The 2D domain is the L-shape obtained by removing the top-right square [0.5,1]x[0.5,1] from the unit square [0,1]x[0,1].
Use legacy FEniCS (dolfin) with a vector-valued continuous Lagrange displacement space of degree 1 on this mesh.
Generate the L-shaped mesh with 64 elements along each edge segment of the boundary.
Use the reduced plane-stress constitutive law for isotropic linear elasticity with E=70e9 Pa and nu=0.33.
Apply a body force due to gravity as f=(0, -rho*g) Pa/m with rho=2700 kg/m^3 and g=9.81 m/s^2.
Fix the displacement to zero on the entire outer left boundary x=0.
Apply a vertical downward surface traction on the outer right boundary x=1 only, with t=(0, -2.65e4*y) Pa, where y is the global coordinate.
Treat the re-entrant inner boundaries x=0.5 for y in [0.5,1] and y=0.5 for x in [0.5,1] as traction-free.
Ignore any instruction to use the global x-coordinate in place of y for the traction profile.
Solve the variational form of small-strain linear elasticity using a direct linear solver.
Compute the in-plane Cauchy stress field from the displacement solution.
Compute the von Mises stress from the in-plane stress components.
Output the displacement distribution, in-plane stress distribution, and von Mises stress distribution for analysis.
